question: In your app directory, both pages/blog/[slug].js and pages/blog/[slug]/comments.js exist. When a user visits /blog/my-post/comments, which file handles the request?
options: pages/blog/[slug].js with slug='my-post/comments'
pages/blog/[slug]/comments.js matches first because it's more specific
Neither; Next.js throws a routing conflict error
pages/blog/[slug].js with slug='my-post'; comments is ignored
explanation: Next.js prioritizes more specific file-based routes; [slug]/comments.js is more specific than [slug].js, so it matches first.

question: You have pages/[...slug].js (catch-all) and pages/settings.js. When you navigate to /settings, which route matches?
options: pages/[...slug].js with slug=['settings']
pages/settings.js matches because it's exact
Both match but settings.js takes precedence
Neither matches; you need pages/settings/index.js
explanation: Exact matches (settings.js) take priority over catch-all routes ([...slug].js) in Next.js routing precedence.

question: You define pages/api/users/[id].js as an API route. A POST to /api/users/123 returns 404. What's the issue?
options: API routes are read-only; you must use GET
req.method check is missing; the file accepts all HTTP verbs by default
API route file must export a default handler that returns res.status
next.config.js must configure API routes explicitly
explanation: API route files must export a default handler function; without it, Next.js cannot invoke the route.

question: In the app directory, you have app/posts/[id]/page.js and app/posts/[id]/layout.js. What happens when /posts/123 is requested?
options: Only page.js renders; layout.js is ignored
layout.js wraps page.js content; both render
They conflict; Next.js throws an error
layout.js is for folder navigation only, not file requests
explanation: Layouts wrap page components; both layout.js and page.js render, with layout as the outer wrapper.

question: You have pages/[[...slug]].js (optional catch-all). A request to / should render this page, but Next.js serves pages/index.js instead. How do you handle root?
options: Delete pages/index.js; optional catch-all replaces it
pages/index.js takes precedence; optional catch-all is for /something/else only
Rename [[...slug]].js to root.js at pages/root/[[...slug]].js
Add explicit route logic in next.config.js
explanation: Optional catch-all routes don't override index.js; they capture child paths like /foo, /foo/bar but not root.

question: In pages/products/[category]/[id].js, you access query params via router.query. On first render, what is router.query?
options: {category: 'electronics', id: '42'}
Empty object {}; params load on useEffect
undefined; you must use getServerSideProps
Null; dynamic routes don't populate query until component mounts
explanation: router.query is populated asynchronously after hydration; it's empty on initial server render.

question: You have pages/api/auth/[...slug].js that delegates to different handlers based on slug[0]. On POST /api/auth/login?debug=1, what is req.query?
options: {slug: ['login'], debug: '1'}
{slug: ['login'], debug: true}
{debug: '1'}; slug is in req.params
Query params are not available in API routes
explanation: Query string params appear in req.query alongside dynamic route params; all values are strings.

question: Between pages/users/[id].js and pages/users/[id]/settings.js, you want only settings.js to render when visiting /users/42/settings. The other should 404. What will happen?
options: Next.js 404s because both match the segment; routes conflict
[id].js wins because it's more general; settings path is ignored
[id]/settings.js matches; it's more specific than [id].js
You must add a check in [id].js to redirect if next segment exists
explanation: Nested dynamic routes follow specificity: [id]/settings.js is more specific than [id].js and will handle the longer path.

question: You have pages/[locale]/index.js. On build, Next.js should generate static HTML for en and fr locales. Without getStaticPaths, what happens?
options: Next.js generates static pages for en and fr automatically
Build succeeds but only SSR is used; no static pre-rendering
Build fails; getStaticPaths is required for dynamic routes
Next.js generates a single HTML and routes dynamically at runtime
explanation: Without getStaticPaths, dynamic routes fall back to SSR; static generation doesn't happen.

question: In app router, both app/(admin)/layout.js and app/layout.js exist. A request to /admin/users is routed through which sequence?
options: app/layout.js → app/(admin)/layout.js → segment component
Only app/(admin)/layout.js wraps the component
Route groups bypass parent layouts; only (admin) layout applies
Both layouts wrap independently; component receives dual context
explanation: Layouts nest hierarchically; a route traverses all parent layouts in order, including the root layout.

question: You use next/link to navigate between routes. Clicking a Link with href='/users/42' triggers a full page reload. What might cause this?
options: next/link only works with 'a' tags; you forgot the 'a' element
The route is dynamic [id].js and Link doesn't support param routes
Client-side navigation is disabled in next.config.js
The page has getServerSideProps or uses middleware that prevents SPA mode
explanation: Link provides soft navigation only if client-side rendering is available; SSR-only pages or certain middleware configurations force full reloads.
